name: decision-not-generation
assertion: Jev is used only where the feature picks a label, a yes/no or a scale position; generated text still comes from the generative model

name: no-hardcoded-model
assertion: The Jev model id is read from the repository's settings, never a string literal in application code

name: key-resolution
assertion: The key comes from the repository's existing LLM key path (per-user key with budget tracking where it exists, else a Total Recall team secret); the key is never logged or printed

name: confidence-gated
assertion: Every automatic action taken on a Jev answer checks confidence against a per-outcome threshold in code; below it the feature asks a human or falls back

name: fallback-exists
assertion: With no key, no configured model, an HTTP error, a timeout or an unreadable response, the feature behaves exactly as it did before Jev

name: human-approval-kept
assertion: Anything that messages customers, deletes data or spends money keeps its human approval step even with a confident Jev answer

name: decision-recorded
assertion: The chosen label, confidence and answering model version are recorded with the feature's result

name: tests-mock-the-call
assertion: pytest covers high-confidence, low-confidence and failure paths with the API call monkeypatched; no test hits the network
